correctness.rationale: Normalize each edge column to e_i+λ_ij f_j. The determinant on a four-cycle vanishes exactly when the two diagonal gain products are equal. In any dependence, the nonzero-coefficient support cannot have a leaf. A simple bipartite graph on at most five edges with all support degrees at least two must be a 4-cycle: with five connected edges it would have at most five vertices, but a 2-by-3 bipartition with no leaves at its three-vertex side requires six edges. Hence all <=5 columns are independent under the gain condition. The six K_2,3 columns occupy five rows, so a weight-six dependence exists. A nonzero left row annihilator would make all gain rows proportional, contradicting a nonzero 2-by-2 minor. The exponent difference (i−k)(j−l) is nonzero modulo the prime p; F_8^× has order seven and z mod z³+z+1 is neither zero nor one (the cubic has no F_2 root). For any K_6,6 filling, six distinct ratios force q−1>=6. At q=7 normalize against one row: two permutations have product-of-values quotient 1, which cannot be the product −1 of a permutation of F_7^×. These are universal proofs; the inspected frozen verify.py records exhaustive concrete checks but was not executed in this review.
